[reviewer finding R4-1, minor] The adjudicated R3-2 repair asked the constructor to remove this blocker, or to say that all asset hashes are concrete and must be recomputed or confirmed by the controller. The new text says hashes are 'either concrete hashes carried over from the previous candidate or CONTROLLER_FILL for assets edited in this repair (facts.json, task.md, private judge_rubric.md)'. That is still false. The three assets edited in this repair carry concrete hashes in tasks[0].assets and input_contract.files: task.md 4d624097..., facts.json ca722f0c..., judge_rubric.md 29b62b61.... A Grep finds exactly one 'CONTROLLER_FILL' in output/package.json, and it is this blocker sentence. The quality_public_surface.json asset records carry the same concrete values. Blocker [5] also says quality_public_surface.json is absent and must be regenerated. That record now exists, and its WC-F36 record contains the repaired caveat text (a Grep for the example (b) clause matches facts.json, package.json and quality_public_surface.json). So blocker [5] is stale as a current-state statement.
Required repair: In package.json and package.constructor_original.json, replace unresolved_blockers[3] with: 'All asset sha256 values are concrete; the controller must recompute/confirm them from the final bytes.' Alternatively, delete the blocker. Reword blocker [5] as historical (record regenerated by the controller) or remove it. No public asset, fact or contract change is needed.
